name: Michelangelo Volpi
current_role: General Partner, Hanabi Capital (co-founded 2025); director of Confluent, Aurora Innovation, Wealthfront and Ferrari N.V.
profile: Milan-born, Tokyo-raised Stanford engineer who became Cisco's chief strategy officer, leading 70+ acquisitions and running its $10B+ routing business. Briefly CEO of Joost, then built Index Ventures' San Francisco office (2009-2024), backing Confluent, Elastic, Scale AI, Aurora and Wealthfront. Now invests in AI/infra via Hanabi Capital.
interesting_fact: As Cisco's M&A chief in the late 1990s he did 70+ acquisitions in under five years; the NYT dubbed him 'The Cisco Whiz Kid' and MIT Technology Review named him an Innovator Under 35 in 1999.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to Japan at age 5-6, attended a Roman Catholic boys' school in Tokyo and is trilingual (Italian, Japanese, English); he started his career in HP's optoelectronics division in 1989 before his Stanford MBA.
notes: Hanabi deploys largely his own capital; AI/infrastructure focus and Aurora (autonomous trucking) board seat make him relevant to data-center/energy themes. Has done podcasts (Uncapped with Jack Altman #52, Microsoft Behind the Tech).

name: William Magnuson
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Braze, Inc. (NASDAQ: BRZE)
profile: Minnesota-born engineer who co-founded Appboy (renamed Braze) in 2011 with Jon Hyman after the pair met at Bridgewater Associates. Initially CTO, he became CEO and took the customer-engagement software company public on Nasdaq in 2021; his wealth comes from his Braze stake.
interesting_fact: Braze traces back to an all-night TechCrunch Disrupt NYC hackathon in 2011, where Magnuson and Jon Hyman built 'Gilty', a browser plugin for reselling flash-sale items left in shopping carts; the buzz led them to investors and to founding Appboy.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bridgewater he worked at Google Research on App Inventor for Android, the visual programming tool built to remove syntax stumbling blocks for computer-science students and later used in schools.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (14 Minutes of SaaS, Mixergy, Battery Ventures). Also mentioned habit of buying cheap domain names for side ideas.

name: Satish Parakh
current_role: Managing Director, Ashoka Buildcon Ltd (Nashik, India)
profile: Civil engineer who joined the Ashoka Group in 1982 and rose to Managing Director of Ashoka Buildcon, one of India's largest highway developers (EPC plus 35+ PPP/BOT road projects). He led its diversification into power transmission/distribution EPC, railways and city gas distribution; his wealth stems from his shareholding in the listed company.
interesting_fact: Ashoka Buildcon was an early mover in India's build-operate-transfer (BOT) road model from the 1990s and has even built a road network for the Housing Development Corporation in the Maldives.
deep_cut_fact: His association with Ashoka began in 1982 and he has received the 'Industry Doyen' award from the Construction Industry Development Council; in interviews he credits the company's in-house highway research facility and its policy of avoiding 'ambitious bidding'.

public_contacts.value: Stellar IR Advisors (investor relations advisor) - vgaurang@stellar-ir.com

notes: Power T&D EPC business is the energy angle. Low public profile beyond trade-press interviews (NBM&CW, Construction World).

name: Zeng Qingrong
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Sichuan Lanjian (Bluesword) Investment Management Co.; founding chairman of Bluesword (Lanjian) Group, retired from its management in 2018
profile: Sichuan entrepreneur and founding chairman of the Bluesword (Lanjian) Group, once nicknamed the 'King of Southwest Beer'. The group built Lanjian beer, Glacier mineral water and Weiyi soy milk; China Resources Snow Breweries took 100% of Lanjian beer in 2007. He left Bluesword beverage management in 2018 and now invests in listed companies via Lanjian Investment.
interesting_fact: Before selling out to China Resources Snow in 2007, his Lanjian beer was so dominant in Sichuan that the market called him the 'Southwest Beer King' (西南啤酒大王).
deep_cut_fact: Beyond beer, he was behind well-known Southwest beverage brands Glacier (冰川) mineral water and Weiyi (唯怡) soy-nut milk; in 2025-26 his investment vehicle became a top-10 shareholder of Sichuan equipment maker Kexin Mechanical & Electrical (300092).
notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Any approach would likely go via Bluesword Group corporate channels (Chengdu). Chinese-language media only.

name: Wang Chaowei
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List in 2007-2008 (~US$120M) with wealth attributed to 'Anshang Group' (mining). No verifiable current information on this person or the company could be found in English- or Chinese-language web sources.
notes: Could not confirm identity, company (安商集团) or current status after several English/Chinese searches; may require Chinese business registry (e.g. national enterprise credit system) research. Not recommended as an outreach target without further verification.

name: Mark Saldanha
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Marksans Pharma Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Science graduate and son of Glenmark founder Gracias Saldanha who took the former Glenmark subsidiary private-label generics business independent and renamed it Marksans Pharma in 2005. He built it into a listed generic/OTC drug maker selling heavily into the US, UK and Australia via acquired subsidiaries; he holds a large controlling stake.
interesting_fact: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, founded by his father in 1977, was named by combining the names of his two sons: Glenn and Mark. Mark later went his own way with Marksans, while brother Glenn runs Glenmark.
deep_cut_fact: Marksans' official bio describes him as a science graduate with hands-on experience across R&D, marketing, production and finance; the company was renamed Marksans Pharma on 10 Oct 2005 after spinning out of Glenmark.
notes: Low media profile; corporate channels are the realistic route. Not an energy/data-center figure.

name: Aj Teague
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Enterprise Products Holdings LLC (general partner of Enterprise Products Partners, NYSE: EPD); announced retirement effective Jan 4, 2027
profile: A. James 'Jim' Teague, Louisiana-raised Navy veteran, spent 22 years at Dow Chemical rising to head of hydrocarbon feedstocks, then joined Enterprise in 1999 via its Tejas NGL acquisition. He became COO, then CEO in 2016 and co-CEO with Randy Fowler in 2020 of one of the largest US midstream pipeline/NGL/export companies. Wealth is from EPD units.
interesting_fact: The Greater Houston Port Bureau named him 2021 Maritime Leader of the Year for his advocacy and financial investment to widen and improve the Houston Ship Channel; he has called his work at Enterprise 'a calling'.
deep_cut_fact: After college (East Texas Baptist University) he served in Vietnam with a Navy attack helicopter squadron and as a naval intelligence officer, then joined Dow Chemical as a pharmaceutical sales rep before moving into its hydrocarbon division.
notes: Strong energy fit (NGLs, petrochemicals, LPG/ethane exports, Permian gas for data centers). Outspoken on energy policy in earnings calls. Retiring Jan 2027, may be more available afterwards. Sits on UH Energy advisory board.

name: David Moreno
current_role: President, FTAI Aviation Ltd. (NASDAQ: FTAI), since Feb 2026
profile: Babson-trained finance executive who spent 2013-2021 on Fortress Investment Group's aviation investment team, then served as FTAI Aviation's COO (2021-2026) leading growth initiatives, acquisitions and partnerships. Named to the newly created President role in Feb 2026, running day-to-day performance as FTAI evolved from aircraft leasing into the leading CFM56/V2500 engine-maintenance platform.
interesting_fact: FTAI launched 'FTAI Power' in Dec 2025, converting CFM56 jet engines (the world's largest aircraft-engine fleet) into ~25 MW aeroderivative gas turbines for AI data centers, targeting 100+ units a year.
deep_cut_fact: CEO Joe Adams credited him as part of the team 'since FTAI's inception' and as key to transforming the company from a leasing platform into an engine-maintenance business; he holds both a B.A. in Business Administration and an M.S. in Accounting from Babson College.
notes: Excellent topical fit: FTAI Power (jet engines repurposed for data-center power). IR head is Alan Andreini per company press releases; route via FTAI IR (ir.ftaiaviation.com). Young executive (~mid-30s), low personal media profile.

name: Noel Edmonds
current_role: Broadcaster and entrepreneur; founder of Positivity Radio; based in New Zealand's South Island
profile: English broadcaster (b. 1948) who rose from Radio Luxembourg and the Radio 1 Breakfast Show to front Multi-Coloured Swap Shop, Noel's House Party (15M+ viewers, creator of Mr Blobby) and Channel 4's Deal or No Deal (2005-16). He built wealth via presenting fees and his Unique Group production/media businesses. Emigrated to New Zealand in 2019, where he launched the Positivity Radio network.
interesting_fact: He was one of the original presenters of BBC's Top Gear in the late 1970s, and later returned to road-test a Ford GT40 (he owned two) because 6ft 5in Jeremy Clarkson couldn't fit in the cockpit.
deep_cut_fact: A licensed helicopter pilot (an early aircraft was registered G-NOEL), he ferried stars to and from Wembley by helicopter during Live Aid in 1985 and flew Phil Collins to Heathrow so he could catch Concorde to play the Philadelphia concert the same day.
notes: Media personality rather than energy/tech founder. Avoid his Lloyds/HBOS dispute and health topics. Lives in New Zealand (Ngatimoti); recent ITV series 'Noel Edmonds' Kiwi Adventure' (2025). Official site lists no direct contact; go via agent/management.

name: Eduardo S Elsztain
current_role: Chairman of IRSA, Cresud, BrasilAgro and Banco Hipotecario (Argentina)
profile: Buenos Aires-born (1960) businessman who, after a 1990 meeting persuaded George Soros to let him manage $10M, built IRSA into Argentina's largest real-estate group (malls, offices, Llao Llao Hotel) and took control of agribusiness Cresud in 1994. He also chairs Brazil's BrasilAgro and mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario, controlling them via his holding company IFISA.
interesting_fact: His career turned on one meeting: in 1990 he landed an hour with George Soros, said he could manage $10M, and Soros replied 'Okay, no problem!'; within four years he had raised $110M and bought Buenos Aires office towers and the Alto Palermo mall.
deep_cut_fact: He saw potential in Buenos Aires' derelict, mice-infested Abasto wholesale market and turned it into Abasto Shopping while keeping its historic facade; and the former Boca Juniors training ground IRSA bought in 1997 finally won approval in 2024 as the Ramblas del Plata waterfront project.
notes: Leading Argentine real estate/agribusiness figure; also active in Jewish community organisations. Spanish-language press covers him widely. Studied medicine and economics at UBA but left to pursue business.
